about: How a menu is drawn once the entries that do not fit are left out (D1600, menus-architecture.md 3.4). One table for the three places that draw a menu: the page (web/app/lib/menus/assemble.ts), the Windows and macOS shell (clients/neutralino/src/menu-actions.ts) and the Linux shell (manifest.visible_only). A menu is its sections; an entry is its label, '~' before it when it is left out, or a submenu. Drawn, '-' is a separator. A menu with nothing left is drawn empty here: each place then adds its one greyed line that says why (D1603).

cases.name: an entry left out in a section
a first section left out: no separator first
a last section left out: no separator last
a middle section left out: no two separators
two sections left out next to each other
a submenu keeps what is left in it
a submenu with nothing left goes, and its section with it
